reasons: Claimed status is 'compliant' with no redline and no comment, which is the expected output shape; nothing actionable is being proposed against the counterparty, so there is no invalid or directionally wrong edit to reject.

The cited text supports the compliance call on the material terms the rule cares about: Article 13 contains express mutual warranties covering authority, compliance with Applicable Laws (13.1.3 Anti-Corruption, 13.1.5 certifications/permits) and SFJ's funding capacity (13.5), and Section 2.2.2 imposes a Protocol/Applicable Law (GCP/GLP/GMP/ICH) performance standard that is the context-appropriate analogue of 'professional and workmanlike'.

The disclaimer does not swallow the express warranties — 13.6.2 opens 'EXCEPT AS OTHERWISE SET FORTH IN THIS ARTICLE 13' — so the walk-away 'AS IS' condition is not triggered, correctly ruling out a deviation.

The failed deterministic check (no 90-day/12-month conformance period) is a phrasing/fit artefact: this is a co-development and funding agreement with no software or deliverable conformance mechanic, and the rationale expressly notes the gap rather than flagging it, consistent with the instruction to note minor sub-elements short of preferred wording.

The rationale correctly declines to disturb 13.6.1 (mutual, and favourable to our party as generator of Research Results) and PB's broader warranties, in line with the rule against flagging clauses that benefit our party or duplicating terms covered by other rules.
